audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Heat, Danger Zone or Overheat anywhere except one passing phrase ("Danger-Zone heat"). The single best window Teemo has in this matchup is never named.
audit.why: Junkyard Titan: at 100% Heat Rumble Overheats — he gains attack speed and bonus damage on basic attacks but cannot cast spells for a few seconds. That is the one state in the game where all of Rumble's damage is basic attacks, and Blinding Dart deletes basic attacks outright. An Overheated, blinded Rumble does literally nothing. Every other window in this lane he has Flamespitter, which the blind cannot touch.
audit.corrected: Hold Blinding Dart for Overheat: he is spell-locked, his only damage is autos, and the blind turns them off.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.enemyWin reads "Rumble wins by landing Scrap Shield, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave", and focus tracks Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining cooldown.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a self-cast shield plus a burst of move speed — there is nothing to land on Teemo, and at a flat 6 seconds it is up for almost every trade, so tracking it tells the player nothing. Rumble wins this lane by walking Flamespitter across Teemo and holding him there with Electro Harpoon slows.
audit.corrected: Rumble wins by holding you inside Flamespitter with Electro Harpoon; track his Heat bar, not a 6-second shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "Q is maxed, so Blinding Shot cooldown is short enough to track his every step-up" at levels 4-5.
audit.why: Two errors. Rank 5 on any ability requires level 9, and more importantly Blinding Dart's cooldown is a flat 7 seconds at every rank — ranking it never changes availability. The number that does change across this window is Flamespitter, 10 seconds at rank 1 down to 6 at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7s at every rank; Flamespitter is what tightens, 10s to 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q is written as "Blinding Shot" in spikes[0], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], early, mid and whys[0].
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json gives slot Q as "Blinding Dart".

audit.whatIsWrong: "Liandry's Angueur" appears three times (spikes[2], late, whys[5]).
audit.why: Not a real item. Liandry's Torment is the name used elsewhere in this dataset.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and mid both tell the player to react to The Equalizer's "channel" / "channel animation".
audit.why: The Equalizer has no channel — Rumble casts it, drags a line, and the flames drop along that line. The kit carries no channel flag for it. What the player actually sees, and can react to, is the targeting line being dragged across the ground; waiting for a channel that never appears is waiting too long.
audit.corrected: React to the targeting line being dragged, and move perpendicular to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ability is written "Electro-Harpoon" and "Equalizer"; the kit names are "Electro Harpoon" and "The Equalizer".
audit.why: Minor, but the site's own ability-name validator flags near-misses, and these are the two Rumble names it will keep catching.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is treated as a single ability throughout.
audit.why: Rumble carries two harpoons at once and they recharge independently, so 'dodge the harpoon' is bad framing — he has a second one and each stacks its own MR shred and slow. Move Quick has to beat both, not one.
audit.corrected: He holds two Electro Harpoons; both slow and both shred MR, so plan the exit around the pair.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[0].why says "AA-poke + E poison wins almost every melee level 1", while content.win[0] is "Rumble" and the content early paragraph correctly explains that Flamespitter beats Teemo's level 1.
audit.why: The two layers contradict each other, and the full layer is the one that is wrong. Flamespitter is online at level 1, it is ability AoE, and Blinding Dart cannot answer it.
audit.corrected: Level 1 is his — Flamespitter is up and the blind does not touch it.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff EVEN / 6.0 difficulty for a 58.55% matchup over 427 games — the strongest win rate in this slice.
audit.why: 58.55% is a clearly winning lane, and the content layer already argues that case correctly. No edit proposed: "EVEN" cannot be replaced inside the length band, and difficulty is partly a how-hard-to-pilot judgement.
audit.corrected: Flagged for the user rather than edited.

edits.before: Rumble owns level 1 because Flamespitter is already online and it does not care about Blinding Shot -- it is ability-based AoE, not an auto-attack, so walking into his range is just accepting free burn damage. Park yourself just outside Flamespitter range and last-hit at Q tip; the blind wastes a cooldown here because he can W straight through it. The moment you hit level 2 and add Toxic Shot, the math reverses: Q him the instant he steps up to flame you, your E poison starts ticking under his Scrap Shield, and W pulls you back out of Electro-Harpoon range before he can slow you into a full trade. Level 3 is where the poke loop becomes suffocating -- you can chip a full Scrap Shield with two or three E autos between his commitments, and he has no way to close on you without burning his harpoon on a target that W-dashes off the shroom you just planted on his exit.
edits.after: Rumble owns level 1 because Flamespitter is already online and it does not care about Blinding Dart -- it is ability-based AoE, not an auto-attack, so walking into his 600 range is just accepting free burn damage. Park yourself outside it and last-hit at Q tip; the blind is wasted here because nothing he throws at you is a basic attack. The moment you hit level 2 and add Toxic Shot the math reverses: E poison ticks under his Scrap Shield, and W pulls you back out of Electro Harpoon range before he can slow you into a full trade. Level 3 is where the poke loop starts to suffocate him -- every spell he casts adds Heat, and if he pushes the bar to 100% he Overheats and cannot cast anything at all for a few seconds. His autos still swing, and they are the only damage he has left. That is the window your blind was saved for.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are where you bank the lead you built in early. Q is maxed, so Blinding Shot cooldown is short enough to track his every step-up; he cannot auto freely AND he cannot walk Flamespitter across you without taking a blind mid-channel. The key threat is Equalizer at 6 -- it is not a duel-finisher but it is a ground-zone that shreds you if you stand in it, so the moment you see the channel animation, hit W and move perpendicular to the drag line. Post-6 your macro improves: drop mushrooms at the river and tribush entrances so Rumble cannot roam without revealing himself, and shove the wave into his tower whenever Equalizer is on cooldown so he has to choose between farming and pressuring you.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are where you bank the lead you built in the early game. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so it is up for every step-up he makes; Flamespitter meanwhile tightens from 10 seconds to 6, which is what actually changes here. The key threat is The Equalizer at 6 -- not a duel-finisher but a ground zone that shreds you if you stand in it, so the instant the targeting line is dragged out, hit W and move perpendicular to it. Post-6 your macro improves: mushrooms at the river and tribush entrances mean Rumble cannot roam unseen, and you shove into his tower whenever The Equalizer is down, which is 130 seconds at its first rank.

By 2+ items the lane is a macro game: Rumble is not a hard scaler but his teamfight Equalizer becomes devastating in 5v5 where you cannot easily W out of a wide AoE, so keep the game in the side lane where your shroom-warded split-push forces him to fight you 1v1, the one format he loses to your poke-and-reposition kit.
edits.after: At first item Liandry's Torment your carry window is wide open -- the burn stacks with Toxic Shot poison and even Rumble's tankier mid-game HP pool melts in a sustained poke sequence while shrooms slow him for the full DoT duration. TWO DERIVED-FLAG FALSE POSITIVES feed this matchup and both should be ignored:
(1) champ-data/_kits/rumble.json flags Scrap Shield (W) with "knockup" and "terrain". Scrap Shield is a self-shield plus a burst of move speed — it displaces nobody and creates nothing.
(2) champ-data/_kits/teemo.json flags Noxious Trap (R) with "knockup". Mushrooms slow and damage; they do not displace.
Because of both, champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json carries a headline for teemo/rumble reading "knockup-enabler: Both sides carry displacement (Noxious Trap (R) vs Scrap Shield (W)) — whoever lands it first owns the trade." That sentence is false on BOTH sides and must not be written into the entry. It is the only missing-interactions row for this matchup, so this matchup effectively has no valid entry in that file.
